newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends higher as bond rallies but techs battered.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends higher as bond rallies but techs battered.

text.p: U.S. blue chips rebounded on Tuesday as fresh economic reports calmed inflation jitters and sent the long bond yield to a 2-1/2 month low, but buying was tempered by fierce selling in technology stocks.

"The bond market liked the economic data and pulled stocks along with it to a point. But there's an overhanging fear of a one-party leadership as of next Tuesday and that will weigh on stocks no matter what the day-to-day news is," said Bob Stovall, president of Stovall/21st Advisers.
After falling 34 Monday, the Dow rose 34 to about 6007.
The S&P 500 surged four to about 702.
But winners outpaced losers by just 12-11 on heavy NYSE volume of 441 million shares.

Wall Street activity was enlivened by New York Yankees manager Joe Torre's ringing of the NYSE opening bell and a ticker tape parade down Broadway, passing within a block of the NYSE. The festivities were in honor of the Yankees clinching the World Series baseball championship.
But the tech-studded Nasdaq Composite slumped 13 points or 1.06 percent to about 1203 amid further tax-loss related selling by mutual funds and a negative analyst comment.

Salomon Brothers said there has been a distinct softening in retail computer sales over the last few weeks, pressuring computer makers and computer retailers. CompUSA shed 5-7/8 to 51-1/2, Tandy lost one to 39, Compaq was off 3-1/8 to 67-1/2, IBM fell 1-5/8 to 125-1/2 and Dell shed 4-7/8 to 76-1/8.

The long bond rallied 1-30/32 in late trading, knocking its yield down to 6.69 percent, matching the close of August 12. If the yield slips further, it would be the lowest since the close of April 4 at 6.66 percent. Bond buying was ignited initially by news that the third-quarter Employee Cost Index rose 0.6 percent, lower than the forecast 0.8 percent rise.
Later, the Conference Board said October U.S. consumer confidence fell to a weaker-than-forecast 106.2 from a revised reading of 111.8 in September.

"People are thinking no Fed tightening for the rest of the year and after the first of (next) year, there might be thinking of a Fed loosening," said Michael LaTronica, director of research at Gruntal & Co. But he noted the rush of economic reports resumes on Wednesday with third-quarter Gross Domestic Product and will be capped by Friday's October jobs.
GDP is seen rising at a 1.8 percent annual rate, cooling down from 4.7 percent second-quarter growth rate.

Paul Rabbitt, a quantitative analyst at Oppenheimer & Co, said the stark contrasts between the Dow gains and Nasdaq losses stemmed from "some pre-election jitters seeking out the safer, longer-term type stocks. We also have end of fiscal year mutual fund tax selling. The core positions don't need to be sold but high-beta bombs for the year might go."
Among individual shares, Electronic Data Systems rose 3-3/4 to 44-7/8 after recent stiff selling as Merrill Lynch upgraded its near-term rating to accumulate from neutral.
National-Oilwell rose 3-1/8 to 20-1/8 in its Wall Street debut.
America Online rose 1-1/8 to 25-3/4 after introducing a new corporate structure and a set of pricing plans deigned to make it more competitive.

Donna Karan lost 3-1/2 to 15-1/4 after the designer forecast break-even fourth-quarter results since current projections for sales in its beauty division continue to be below plan for the period. Analysts cut earnings estimates.

Interest-rate sensitive shares bounded higher as the long bond yield headed south. Wells Fargo rose 3-5/8 to 264-1/8, Freddie Mac added 2-1/8 to 99-3/8, Citicorp was up 2-3/8 to 97-3/8 and Fannie Mae added 7/8 to 37-7/8.
DSP Communications tumbled 17-1/8 to 35-1/4 after announcing plans to merge with Proxim Inc, up 2-51/64 to 21-1/2, in a deal valued at $400 million.

Premonos Technology slumped nine to 7-5/8, an all-time low, after announcing a quarterly loss and the resignation of a top executive. The company also warned that earnings before acquisition costs on a per share basis for 1996 will be somewhat below those of 1995.
SyStemix lost 1-3/4 to 14-1/4 after independent directors rejected an unsolicited offer by Sandoz Ltd to acquire at $17 a share the outstanding shares of Systemix that Sandoz does not already own.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 12.84 to 1203.05.
The S&P 500 index rose 4.24 to 701.50.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
